summary: Defines MIB objects for managing uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Gauges for checking the battery backup that keeps computers on during a blackout.

questions: how do you monitor a ups with snmp
what alarms can a ups raise
subtitle: SNMP objects for monitoring and managing uninterruptible power supplies.

tldr.problem: Uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) are critical for keeping networks and servers running during blackouts, but administrators need a way to monitor their status remotely and receive alerts when battery runs low.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1628 defines a set of SNMP management objects (MIB) organized into groups for device identification, battery status, input/output power, bypass mode, alarms, testing, control commands, and configuration. Tools like SNMP managers can query these objects to track voltage, current, temperature, remaining runtime, and raise alarms.
tldr.outcome: The UPS MIB became the standard way to integrate UPS systems into network management platforms, enabling automated monitoring and alerting across heterogeneous hardware from different vendors.

today: RFC 1628 is a Standards Track specification and remains in use today. It provides the baseline UPS MIB; vendor-specific extensions have been added over time, but all vendors implement the core objects defined here for compatibility.

sections.title: What Is a UPS MIB?
sections.content:
A Management Information Base (MIB) is a standardized vocabulary of data objects that network devices expose via SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol). An SNMP manager can query these objects to monitor device state and receive notifications of problems.

RFC 1628 defines the UPS MIB: a set of objects that represent the state of an uninterruptible power supply. An administrator can write a script that queries the UPS every minute to check battery charge, estimate runtime remaining, and raise an alert if charge drops below 25 percent. Vendors implement this MIB in their UPS firmware so that any SNMP management tool (Nagios, Prometheus, OpenNMS) can talk to any UPS, regardless of manufacturer. Before standards like this, each vendor had a proprietary API, forcing operators to run separate monitoring for each brand.
sections.eli5: Imagine a thermometer that you can read from across town through the internet. The MIB is the agreement about what the thermometer measures and what words mean "hot" or "cold". Every UPS obeys the same agreement, so one monitoring dashboard works for all of them.

sections.title: The Nine Object Groups
sections.content:
The UPS MIB organizes about 60 objects into nine groups, each corresponding to a physical or functional part of the UPS.

Device Identification holds static facts: manufacturer name, model, software version, and a configurable name and description of attached devices. Battery objects report status (normal, low, depleted), estimated charge percentage (0–100%), estimated minutes until depletion under current load, voltage, current, and temperature. Input describes the AC power coming in: frequency, voltage, and power on each input line, plus a counter of how many times input went out of tolerance. Output mirrors that for the power going to protected equipment: voltage, current, power, and percent load.

Bypass objects report whether the UPS is in bypass mode (AC passing straight through without battery/inverter). Alarm objects represent discrete alerts: battery low, on battery, battery depleted, loss of input, and so forth; reading an alarm object tells you whether it is currently active or inactive. Test objects allow an operator to run diagnostics (battery test, deep discharge test) and read results and progress. Control objects let you turn the UPS on/off or cause specific actions like switching to battery. Configuration holds tunable parameters like the voltage low and high thresholds, the delay before shutdown, and minimum battery runtime.
sections.eli5: The MIB is organized like a user manual's table of contents: Chapter 1 is "what is this machine", Chapter 2 is "battery status", Chapter 3 is "input power", and so on. Each object is one sentence you can read, like "battery charge is 75 percent" or "we are currently on battery power".

sections.title: Battery Status and Estimation
sections.content:
The battery group is the heart of UPS monitoring. The upsBatteryStatus object reports one of four states: unknown (UPS cannot determine state), batteryNormal (estimated run-time exceeds the configured low-battery threshold), batteryLow (remaining run-time is below the threshold, typically a few minutes), or batteryDepleted (UPS cannot sustain the load even if power is lost now).

An SNMP manager typically configures a threshold in the Configuration group (e.g., upsConfigLowBattTime) to define what "low" means for this site. Common choices are 5 or 10 minutes. When remaining time drops to that threshold, upsBatteryStatus flips from batteryNormal to batteryLow, and the manager can page an operator or trigger a graceful shutdown.

The upsEstimatedMinutesRemaining object is calculated by the UPS firmware based on current power draw and battery charge. A UPS delivering 5 kW from a 100 kWh battery has approximately 20 minutes left. The estimate becomes unreliable if load changes suddenly, so it is a guide rather than a guarantee.
sections.eli5: The UPS looks at how fast the battery is draining and calculates: at this rate, I have 10 minutes left. When the timer hits the low-battery threshold you set, it rings the alarm so you have time to shut down gracefully instead of losing power suddenly.

sections.title: Monitoring Input and Output Power
sections.content:
The Input and Output groups describe the electrical characteristics of AC power. Both measure voltage (in RMS volts), current (in 0.1-amp increments), frequency (in 0.1-Hz increments), and true power (in watts).

The upsInputLineBads counter increments each time input transitions from out-of-tolerance to in-tolerance or vice versa. If this counter grows rapidly, it signals an unstable power source (a weak utility feed, a failing generator, or a manufacturing environment with heavy inductive loads). The output frequency and voltage depend on the upsOutputSource: when on battery, the UPS's inverter generates 50 or 60 Hz (depending on region) from the battery voltage; when on normal utility input, output frequency tracks the input.

The upsOutputPercentLoad is expressed as a percentage of the UPS's rated power capacity. A value above 100 percent is possible for brief periods on some UPS models (overload capacity). A value approaching 100 percent signals that the estimated runtime will be shorter because the UPS is delivering more power.
sections.eli5: Input power is what comes from the wall or generator; output power is what the UPS delivers to your servers. Both have voltage, current, and frequency. If input is unstable (goes out-of-tolerance a lot), your UPS is working hard. If output load is high, the battery drains faster.

sections.title: Alarms, Tests, and Control
sections.content:
The Alarm group defines discrete alarm objects, each representing a condition the UPS detects. Possible alarms include upsAlarmBatteryBad (self-test failed), upsAlarmOnBattery (utility input lost), upsAlarmLowBattery (estimated runtime is very low), upsAlarmDepletedBattery (cannot sustain load), upsAlarmInputBad (input out of tolerance), and others. Reading an alarm object tells you whether it is currently present.

The Test group permits remote testing of the battery via SNMP. An operator or monitoring script can request a battery test, and the UPS will execute a discharge cycle to verify battery health. The upsTestResult object reports pass, fail, or in-progress, and upsTestPercentComplete tracks progress.

The Control group allows remote power control: shutting down the UPS, turning it back on after a delay, or switching to battery mode for testing. These are powerful operations guarded by SNMP access control so that only authorized administrators can trigger them.
sections.eli5: Alarms are warning lights: battery is bad, we're on battery power, battery is almost gone. Tests let you check if the battery actually works by running it. Control commands let you turn the machine on and off from the network, but only if you have permission.

layers.label: Configuration & Control
layers.detail: Tunable parameters and commands for on/off, testing

layers.label: Alarm
layers.detail: Boolean flags for active problems (low battery, input bad, etc.)

layers.label: Bypass & Output
layers.detail: AC bypass status and output voltage, current, frequency, load

layers.label: Input
layers.detail: Incoming AC power: voltage, current, frequency, line quality

layers.label: Battery
layers.detail: Status, charge percent, voltage, temperature, estimated runtime

layers.label: Device Identification
layers.detail: Manufacturer, model, software version, device name
